summary: Insimul's half of the supported cell. NO CELL IS SUPPORTED TODAY: on every engine at least one of the four axes is unstated, unbuilt, or disjoint from Talos's published claim. This file says which, and how each value was measured — it does not claim support Insimul has not earned.

contract.rule: A supported cell is the INTERSECTION of two per-minor artifact matrices — Insimul's and the counterparty's. A cell is supported only when BOTH projects ship a per-minor artifact for it. A cell either project leaves unbuilt is not a supported cell, however green the other project's tests are.
consumer_procedure: 1. Read the four Insimul axes for the engine from `engines[].axes` here.
2. Read the counterparty's per-minor claim from its own matrix (`counterparty.matrix`).
3. The cell is supported iff every axis has status `verified` on both sides AND the engine minors agree.
4. Any axis at `unstated`, `declared` or `unverified` yields cell status `unsupported` — refuse before the run, not during it (see the refuse-at-hello contract).

axis_status_vocabulary.verified: a per-minor artifact exists and was exercised on that minor; a measurement, not a declaration
axis_status_vocabulary.declared: a manifest states the value, but no artifact on that minor has been exercised
axis_status_vocabulary.unstated: the artifact that should carry the value does not carry it — the axis is silent, not permissive
axis_status_vocabulary.unverified: the value is known but its support claim has never been tested

cell_status_vocabulary.supported: both matrices ship a per-minor artifact for this cell and both are verified
cell_status_vocabulary.unsupported: at least one axis is not verified on at least one side
cell_status_vocabulary.disjoint: both sides state a value and the values do not overlap — not merely untested, actively incompatible

axes.label: Engine minor
axes.insimul_settles_with: jq -r .EngineVersion unreal/Insimul.uplugin; jq -r .unity unity/package.json; grep -h 'compatibility_minimum\|config/features' godot/gdextension/insimul.gdextension godot/templates/project/project.godot

axes.label: C ABI
axes.insimul_settles_with: cat native/VERSION; grep -n 'INSIMULCORE_ABI_VERSION' native/corebridge/src/insimulcore.c; grep -rn 'ExpectedNativeSemver\|ExpectedAbiSemver' unity unreal godot
axes.note: TWO C surfaces share this axis, not one: libinsimul (12 entry points, native/include/insimul.h) and libinsimulcore (5 entry points, native/corebridge/include/insimulcore.h). libinsimul has NO compiled-in ABI symbol — only insimul_version(), a semver+sha build stamp read off the dist VERSION file — so the axis is proxied by the library semver on MAJOR.MINOR. libinsimulcore does carry INSIMULCORE_ABI_VERSION, but it is not written to the dist stamp, so it is only checkable against a loaded library at runtime.

axes.label: Save/snapshot format
axes.note: NAMING COLLISION, called out rather than conflated. The axis §7.7 means is the save/snapshot FORMAT compatibility gate, which in Insimul is SAVE_FILE_VERSION (server/rust/insimul-server/src/save_file.rs). Insimul separately has `snapshotVersion` in babylon/packages/core/src/world-snapshot-version.ts, which is a per-world monotonic STRUCTURE counter compared against worldVersion with a MAX_COMPATIBLE_VERSION_GAP of 50 — a different quantity with a colliding name. An adapter that publishes the world counter as capabilities.insimul.snapshot_version publishes the wrong axis.

axes.label: Plugin / bridge build
axes.owner: insimul (Insimul plugin) and talos (Talos plugin + TBP protocol)
axes.insimul_settles_with: jq -r .VersionName unreal/Insimul.uplugin; jq -r .version unity/package.json; grep -n '^version=' godot/addons/insimul/plugin.cfg
axes.note: The Insimul-side plugin version is measurable today. The `insimul-talos-bridge` artifact that would carry a TBP version range does not exist in any engine repo yet (BRIDGE §7.9, Insimul item 2), so the TBP half of this axis has no Insimul-side declaration at all.

counterparty.access: read-only; copied here for comparison, never edited from this repo

measured_from.how: read-only inspection of the submodule working trees at the gitlink SHAs this branch pins

cell.why: Talos publishes a green claim at 4.6.0 (282 tests). Insimul's GDExtension declares compatibility_minimum 4.2 and has NOT been built for any minor — the descriptor's bin/ paths are declarative, so there is no per-minor native artifact on either 4.3 or 4.6. §7.7: a cell without both artifacts is not a supported cell.

engine_version.note: compatibility_minimum is a floor, not a support claim, and the two files disagree about the intended minor (4.2 vs 4.3). Neither is 4.6.

c_abi.source: godot/ — no expected-ABI constant exists (grep for ExpectedNativeSemver/ExpectedAbiSemver finds nothing outside unity/)
c_abi.note: The Godot addon binds libinsimul through the GDExtension without declaring which libinsimul semver it was written against, so skew here is undetectable from the manifest. Unity declares this; Godot does not.

snapshot_version.note: Workspace-wide, not per-engine: one save format serves all runtimes. Never round-tripped through the Godot runtime, so the value is known and the claim is untested.

plugin_version.note: godot/package.json declares no version field. No insimul-talos-bridge artifact exists, so no TBP range is declared.

cell.why: Both sides state a value and they do not overlap: unity/package.json declares Unity 2022.3 as the minimum editor, while Talos's only green Unity claim is 6000.3.21f1 (108 tests). The intersection of {2022.3-and-up as declared} with {6000.3, as tested} is untested on Insimul's side and stated nowhere as a support claim. This is the §7.7 skew, visible before a run.

engine_version.note: A UPM minimum-editor declaration, not a tested-on claim; nothing records a Unity minor Insimul was exercised on.

c_abi.note: The ONLY engine that states this axis. Compatibility keys on MAJOR.MINOR; unity/scripts/fetch-native.sh cross-checks the fetched libinsimul stamp against ExpectedNativeSemver and warns on drift, while libinsimulcore's ABI is checked only at runtime by InsimulCore.VerifyAbiVersion(). Matches native/VERSION (0.1.0).

snapshot_version.note: Never round-tripped through the Unity runtime.

plugin_version.note: No insimul-talos-bridge artifact exists, so no TBP range is declared.

cell.why: Neither project has published anything. Insimul.uplugin carries NO EngineVersion key at all — the axis is silent, and a silent axis is not a permissive one. Talos's UE binary matrix is planned at 5.5–5.8 × Win64/Linux/Mac but unpublished [TBP §4.3]. There is nothing to intersect.

engine_version.source: unreal/Insimul.uplugin — `jq -r .EngineVersion` yields null; the key is absent
engine_version.note: This is §7.7's settling command returning nothing, which is the finding rather than a gap in the measurement. UE treats an absent EngineVersion as 'any', which is exactly the silent-permissive failure the refuse-at-hello contract exists to convert into a refusal.

c_abi.note: Same gap as Godot: the plugin does not declare which libinsimul semver it was built against.

snapshot_version.note: Never round-tripped through the Unreal runtime.

plugin_version.note: No insimul-talos-bridge artifact exists, so no TBP range is declared.

not_tracked_by_talos: c_abi — Talos's clean-room posture means it never links libinsimul and does not model this axis; it is Insimul's to declare in capabilities.insimul.core_version.
snapshot_version — Talos checkpoints through whatever the game exposes; the save FORMAT gate is Insimul's, surfaced as capabilities.insimul.snapshot_version.
The Insimul plugin version — Talos's matrix records engine minors and its own plugin, not third-party plugin builds.

refuse_at_hello.rule: An adapter declares all four axes in `hello` and is REFUSED at the handshake when any of them falls outside this matrix — not at first use. A refusal at handshake is something the Conductor can plan around; a refusal at first restore_checkpoint is a wasted run. A checkpoint is only valid within its snapshot_version, so a persisted archive entry from a skewed build is INVALIDATED, never restored.
refuse_at_hello.cases: scripts/engine-versions/fixtures (21 cases; scripts/engine-versions/selftest-hello.sh proves the gate both refuses and admits)
decision_order: 1. protocol — a TBP major the adapter does not implement is refused before any axis is read
2. engine — an engine with no row in this matrix is refused
3. capabilities.insimul — a hello without it is refused, never degraded into (§7.8's dangerous row)

4. the four axes in order (engine_version, c_abi, snapshot_version, plugin_version): an axis whose published status is not `verified` refuses regardless of what the build reports; then the value is compared
5. the counterparty claim — same engine, same minor, or the intersection is empty
6. the published cell status, as a backstop: if the axes pass and the cell says otherwise, the matrix wins
refuse_at_hello.first_blocking_axis_wins: One refusal carries ONE token — the first blocking reason in decision order. Order is contract, not taste: two adapters refusing the same build must produce the same token, or Conductor-side attribution drifts per engine.

error_envelope.note: Talos freezes its top-level `code` enum and lets `data.sub_code` grow freely [talos:docs/03-engine-bridge.md §2.11], so every Insimul token is a SUB-code; Insimul does not mint top-level codes it does not own. NOT_DECLARED (-32003) is the closest frozen code — the build does not declare a combination the matrix supports — and it is not retryable, because waiting does not rebuild a plugin. Caveat: talos:addons/talos/core/refusals.gd classifies module refusals against a fixed NOT_DECLARED_REASONS list that contains no insimul_* reason, so a refusal routed through that classifier lands on INVALID_PARAMS (-32602) instead. Until that list grows, the adapter constructs the error itself.

checkpoint_rule.statement: A persisted checkpoint archive entry is restorable only if it is stamped with the axes AND those axes match the published matrix. Every uncertainty resolves to `invalidate`.
checkpoint_rule.why: Go-Explore archives persist checkpoints across runs [TBP §2.6], so an archive built before a core upgrade outlives it. Restoring a stale-format snapshot that happens to parse is the worst available failure — it produces a world that is subtly not the world the archive believed it had.
checkpoint_rule.carrier: TBP's save_checkpoint response is additionalProperties:false over {id, tier, frame, latency_ms, bytes, level} — no version field. The stamp is therefore the adapter's own archive-side metadata, not a wire field, which is why an unstamped archive is the default rather than the exception.

carrier.finding: capabilities.insimul — the block BRIDGE §3.1 proposes and this whole contract rides on — does NOT validate against tbp/1.x today. hello_response.schema.json declares `capabilities` with additionalProperties:false and no `insimul` key, and its own description says unknown keys are REJECTED rather than ignored, precisely so a misspelled flag cannot masquerade as a deliberate absence.
carrier.reproduce: validate a valid tbp hello_response fixture with capabilities.insimul added, against that schema: "Additional properties are not allowed ('insimul' was unexpected) ['result','capabilities']". Verbatim command in docs/REFUSE_AT_HELLO.md.
carrier.consequence: The contract is specified and executable here, and has nowhere to travel on the wire until Talos registers capabilities.insimul in an additive minor. That is a counterparty ask (BRIDGE §7.9), not an Insimul-side workaround: a namespaced block added by the schema owner is additive, while anything Insimul adds unilaterally is a schema violation the peer is required to reject.

insimul_hello_malformed.means: the handshake carried no result object at all; nothing was checked because nothing was readable

insimul_tbp_protocol_unknown.means: a TBP major this adapter does not implement. Not a skewed axis — a different protocol, and guessing at an unknown envelope is how a misparse becomes a finding
insimul_tbp_protocol_unknown.unblock: upgrade the adapter to a TBP major it declares

insimul_engine_unknown.means: the engine has no row in the published matrix. Unpublished is not 'probably fine'
insimul_engine_unknown.unblock: publish a row for the engine in docs/supported-versions.json

insimul_capabilities_absent.means: a hello with no capabilities.insimul — BRIDGE §7.8's dangerous row, where Talos would run against what looks like an ordinary game and file findings while the ground truth sits unread
insimul_capabilities_absent.unblock: install insimul-talos-bridge, or run the game as an ordinary Talos target with no Insimul profile

insimul_checkpoint_unstamped.means: the archive carries no version stamp. This is the DEFAULT, not an exotic case: TBP's save_checkpoint response carries {id, tier, frame, latency_ms, bytes, level} and no version field, so an adapter that does not stamp the axes itself produces exactly this
insimul_checkpoint_unstamped.unblock: stamp the four axes into the archive entry at save_checkpoint time

insimul_checkpoint_axis_uncheckable.means: the matrix publishes no value for an axis the archive must be compared on (Godot and Unreal declare no expected C ABI anywhere). Uncheckable is not matching
insimul_checkpoint_axis_uncheckable.unblock: declare an expected value for the axis in the engine plugin, as Unity does with ExpectedNativeSemver/ExpectedAbiSemver

insimul_checkpoint_snapshot_version_abse.means: the archive is stamped, but not on the snapshot_version axis. Half a stamp is not a stamp

insimul_checkpoint_snapshot_version_skew.means: the archive was written under a different snapshot_version. Go-Explore archives persist ACROSS runs, so an entry outlives the upgrade that invalidated it
insimul_checkpoint_snapshot_version_skew.unblock: discard the entry and re-explore; a stale-format snapshot that parses is worse than no snapshot

insimul_checkpoint_c_abi_absent.means: the archive is stamped, but not on the c_abi axis. Half a stamp is not a stamp

insimul_checkpoint_c_abi_skew.means: the archive was written under a different c_abi. Go-Explore archives persist ACROSS runs, so an entry outlives the upgrade that invalidated it
